messages.subject: [statnet_help] network question
messages.body_plain:
Dear Statnet help,

I have been having a problem with network visualization while using statnet
and I can't find any threads on R postings that are relevant so I thought I
would ask you, even though it might be a network package problem.

Whenever I try to plot networks with different edge colours, given as a
matrix, the edges are suddenly pastel shades and a different style. Even if
I try plot(network, edge.col=matrix, edge.lty=0) the edges will be pastel
colors. I have looked in the documentation and can't find why this is and
the edge.lty and edge.lwd commands don't seem to work. Have you come across
this problem and do you know how I could fix it?

I'm running R Version 2.4.0 GUI 1.17 (3868), network package Version 1.1-1,
sna version 1.3, and statnet Version 1.0-11, on a Mac PowerBook G4.

Thank you. I'd really appreciate some advice...

Caroline Buckee

Population Biology of Infectious Diseases
Department of Zoology
University of Oxford

messages.body_plain:
Hi, Caroline -

Caroline Buckee wrote:
> Dear Statnet help,
> 
> I have been having a problem with network visualization while using 
> statnet and I can't find any threads on R postings that are relevant so 
> I thought I would ask you, even though it might be a network package 
> problem.
> 
> Whenever I try to plot networks with different edge colours, given as a 
> matrix, the edges are suddenly pastel shades and a different style. Even 
> if I try plot(network, edge.col=matrix, edge.lty=0) the edges will be 
> pastel colors. I have looked in the documentation and can't find why 
> this is and the edge.lty and edge.lwd commands don't seem to work. Have 
> you come across this problem and do you know how I could fix it?
> 
> I'm running R Version 2.4.0 GUI 1.17 (3868), network package Version 
> 1.1-1, sna version 1.3, and statnet Version 1.0-11, on a Mac PowerBook G4.
> 
> Thank you. I'd really appreciate some advice...
> 

I haven't seen this problem before; it doesn't seem to be affecting my 
installation.  Can you post a snippet of the offending code?

Thanks,

-Carter

PS. The lty argument to plot.network/gplot controls the line type for 
the border of the edge, not the edge itself.  (Edges are actually drawn 
as very thin polygons, for fascinating but suitably arcane reasons which 
need not concern us here.)  In some cases, however, the polygons may be 
so thin that only the outer line is visible -- thus can one obtain the 
effect of dotted edges without actually drawing them as such.  In any 
event, lty=0 does not mean "draw no edges," at least not since sna 
version 0.5 or thereabouts (when the new gplot was introduced).  Those 
who are interested should take a look at gplot.arrow/network.arrow and 
polygon to see how the code is written.
